identity: Neutral cis-HNNH (Z-diazene), CAS 15626-42-3, singlet C2v ground state. It is distinct from trans-HNNH and isodiazene H2NN. The JANAF H-061 evaluation and FastChem record explicitly identify cis. NASA N2H2 explicitly combines trans, cis and 1,1 isomers in equilibrium, and therefore cannot be a single-cis comparator.
recommendation: Resolve the identity exclusion and prepare a retained-thermal ATcT energy candidate for cis-HNNH as a separate follow-up. Do not replace the cis row with the NASA equilibrium-isomer mixture.
science: The original JANAF page 1321 was visually inspected. Its 1965 evaluation uses estimated geometry, partly estimated vibrational frequencies and a broad energy uncertainty, and states that cis thermochemical properties are adopted. ATcT 1.228 gives Hf(0)=228.92 kJ/mol versus the old JANAF value near 220.00 kJ/mol. Consistent atomic balancing yields a physical atomization-energy decrease of 9.259 kJ/mol, reducing retained-fit K to 0.47597 at 1500 K and 0.75699 at 4000 K. Current/JANAF agrees within 1.68%, isolating source energy rather than a fit transcription failure.
modern: The full Martin-Taylor benchmark author manuscript was inspected. Its high-level anharmonic calculation gives a cis-minus-trans 0 K gap of 5.21 kcal/mol and explicitly separates three isomers; it is a major contributor to the current ATcT cis value, not independent validation of the same network. The full 2024 isotope-spectroscopy paper distinguishes cis/trans/iso IR bands at the CCSD level; it is not a complete high-temperature thermodynamic evaluation and its qualitative equilibrium discussion does not remove cis from the 1500-4000 K network.
importance: Diazene participates in nitrogen-hydrogen reaction chemistry. Its cis inventory is tiny on this hot equilibrium grid; reaction intermediates and non-equilibrium populations are outside the inventory assessment.
conventions: JANAF uses electronic weight one and rotational symmetry number two for the cis molecule. No trans or isodiazene statistical multiplier belongs in that single-isomer function. A future state-based thermal model must handle the strong resonances described in the benchmark paper and explicitly normalize nuclear-spin weights.
followup: Build an exact cis ATcT-minus-JANAF physical energy shift while retaining the inherited thermal function and fitting residual; then perform current-network substitutions. A full thermal replacement needs a cis-resolved rovibrational model, not the NASA mixture. The available original evaluation and benchmark paper suffice for this scoped source review without a mandatory new literature request.
